text: Hello and welcome to our LIVE coverage of this Premier League fixture between Everton and Aston Villa at Goodison Park!

It wasn't so long ago for Toffees supporters since the Halcyon Days of four straight Premier League victories (in fact it was only last month...) a run that helped to eradicate the 10-point deduction for a breach of Profit and Sustainability rules - a punishment the club have challenged.

Since then, though, it's six games without a win in all competitions and Sean Dyche's side are outside of the bottom three only on goal difference after Luton Town drew with Burnley on Friday, so three points here would be most welcome.

In contrast, Villa are absolutely flying and have lost only once in their previous 13 outings in all competitions and even in that one they squandered a two-goal lead to lose 3-2 at Manchester United.
A win today would see Unai Emery's men go level on points with table-toppers Liverpool, who are next in Premier League action on January 21 at Bournemouth.
A big incentive then to head back to the Midlands with three points in the bag,
Dyche makes two changes to his Everton side and the big news is that Doucoure is back another a month-long absence with a hamstring injury.
Everton have not won in his absence and he comes in for McNeil, who is fit enough for the bench after going off injured in the 0-0 FA Cup draw with Crystal Palace last time out.
The other change is in goal where Pickford reclaims the gloves from Virginia.
Calvert-Lewin starts after having his red versus the Eagles overturned on appeal.
Emery goes with four alterations from the side that defeated Middlesbrough in the FA Cup last week.
Cash, Dendoncker, Ramsey and Duran all drop to the bench, with Carlos, Luiz, Diaby and Watkins all named in the starting XI.
It's a big day for Toffees skipper Coleman today, The veteran full-back will become Everton's record Premier League appearance maker when he takes to the field today.
Kick-off is fast approaching in this one...
Referee David Coote blows his whistle and we are underway at Goodison Park!
It's been a pretty sedate opening to this one so far, McGinn crosses from deep on the left towards the far end of the penalty area where Bailey slips and is unable to gain control of the ball.
Everton have the first corner of the game after good work from Harrison, who swings over the delivery left footed straight into the hands of Martinez in the Villa goal.
Harrison is looking pretty lively for Everton, his deep cross the from the right reaches Danjuma who comically slices his volley.
The ball eventually comes to Mykolenko, who slashes wildly over the top.
Oh dear! Pure comedy from Villa as Martinez takes a short one to Douglas Luiz, who is immediately under pressure from Onana.
The Belgian midfielder almost steals it but ends up fouling Martinez on the slide tackle.
It's a huge let-off for the visitors.
McGinn catches Doucoure late with a challenge that looked a lot worse on the slow-motion replay and he rightly escapes a yellow card.
Douglas Luiz puts his team under pressure with a sloppy foul on Branthwaite.
It gives Everton the chance to take a shot at goal from the free-kick from around 25 yards but Garner shoots straight at the wall.
Oooft more promising play from the home side.
Branthwaite plays a wonderful pass out to Danjuma on the left and his low delivery is well cut out by Moreno in the area.
Villa haven't settled at all into this game yet.
Since their return to the Premier League in 2019, Aston Villa have remained unbeaten in their nine league games against Everton (W7 D2), keeping six clean sheets and winning the last five in a row.
Villa finally spark into some life.
Watkins is played in behind the Everton defence and has a chance to work Pickford, but can only shoot straight at his England team-mate.
He'll feel he might have done a bit better with that one.
Have Villa weathered that early pressure? Luiz finds Moreno down the left flank and the full-back's low ball needs intervention from Mykolenko.
There have been a few signs of life from the away side in the last couple of minutes.

GOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOAL FOR VILLA! Or is it? McGinn wins a corner off Tarkowski on the left, they take it short and it's worked back to Bailey, who finds Moreno on the edge of the D and the full-back hits an excellent low drive on the half-volley into the bottom-right corner.
But the VAR are going to look at this one.
Well, after what felt like a lifetime, the goal is chalked out.
Everton were appealing for offside against Bailey but Danjuma might have been keeping him on when he was on the ground.
Lenglet might have also been in the line of vision of Pickford when Moreno struck it.
The long and short of it is that this one is still locked at 0-0 and Everton have a reprieve.
Villa continue to press the issue here, though, and Moreno wins another corner in a battle with Coleman.
It's taken short again but McGinn's eventual delivery is finally cleared despite a few nervy Everton moments.
Since that promising opening, Everton have really struggled to impose themselves on this game.
Moreno has been a thorn in the side of the Toffees' backline, he's looked Villa's most potent weapon so far.
What on earth is Pickford thinking there? McGinn again tries to find Moreno on the left but he's miles away from goal.
That doesn't stop the England keeper dashing out to try and get there but luckily Coleman already dealt with the danger.
That could have ended up far worse for Everton.
WHAT A SAVE! That's more like it from Pickford.
Villa worked the ball up to Watkins whose shot was going wide.
Eventually it's re-worked, though, and Bailey angles one at the near post from the right-hand side of the area.
Pickford is down brilliantly low to his left to palm the ball away.
Great save but Villa are now well on top here.
There's a break in play here as Watkins challenges Tarkowski, who has a cut after being caught by the forward's arm.
Watkins goes into the book for catching Tarkowski in that aforementioned aerial challenge.
Tarkowski is eventually okay to carry on after getting his cut cleaned up.
It's a bit of a harsh yellow in all honesty.

No player has more Premier League assists this season than Aston Villa’s Ollie Watkins (8), while only Mohamed Salah (22) and Erling Haaland (18) have more goals and assists combined than the Villa frontman (9 goals, 8 assists).
He’s only the fifth different English player with 8+ goals and 8+ assists in his team’s opening 20 games of a season, and first since Harry Kane in 2020-21 (12 goals, 11 assists).
Everton finally show a bit of life.
Some aggressive hassling eventually leads to Danjuma getting a run into the penalty area.
His shot eventually gets the corner from Carlos, but it comes to nothing.
This one is on a knife-edge at the moment.
Villa will be disappointed not to be ahead after that earlier disallowed goal and the longer Everton stay alive in the contest the more their hopes grow of stealing a march in the game.
Watkins has been a real thorn in the side of the Everton defence.
On more than one occasion Villa have gone pretty direct to try and find him early.
Thus far it hasn't quite come to fruition but the more he probes the more likely he is to eventually get another opportunity.
There's another break in play here as Moreno takes a smack in the face (from a ball not a player).
He has a bit of a bloody nose so he'll have to get that cleaned up.
Moreno again tries to get in down the left but it's good work from Coleman to defend the danger and it again comes to nought.
OH THAT SHOULD BE THE OPENER! Everton have soaked up so much pressure but they launch a counter with Danjuma's outside-of-the-boot throughball setting Calvert-Lewin through one-on-one.
The striker shoots straight at Martinez when he should have buried it.
The goalkeeper is called into action again soon after to deny Garner from the edge of the area.
A big moment in this game that.
Everton will be deperately disappointed not to be ahead but it has galvanised them a little at the end of this half.
Mykolenko has a tame volley straight at Martinez from Onana's deep delivery, but he was offside anyway.

There were eight minutes added on due to the few stoppages we've had in this first half so if either side is going to head into the break with the advantage then they're going to have to do something pretty quickly.
HALF-TIME: EVERTON 0-0 ASTON VILLA
Coote blows his whistle for half-time and we are goalless at Goodison Park.
Villa thought they had the lead through an expertly taken strike from Moreno but it was chalked off after a lengthy VAR check for offside.
The visitors probably had the better of the play but Everton have had the better chances, as shown by the fact the hosts have an xG of 1.00 to Villa's 0.29.
The best of those went to Calvert-Lewin at the end of the half, he looked a striker out of form and ultimately he wasn't able to make the breakthrough.

So, the big question looking ahead to the second half is who can grab this one by the scruff of the neck and emerge victorious? Villa need to be a little more incisive if they are to do so, while for Everton it's a case of being clinical when the opportunities do present themselves.
It's all to play for, so don't go anywhere folks...
Another blast of the whistle from Coote signals the start of the second half!
Carlos goes in the book and it's a very silly one.
There's a throw-in over on the right and the centre-back just chucks the ball away to buy a bit of time to reset.
He's walking a bit of a needless tightrope now for that.
Ouch! That's very nasty.
Tarkowski and Mykolenko both go up in the air trying to defend the same ball and there's a collision of heads that leaves the Everton team-mates both in need of medical attention.
Mykolenko has definitely come off worse in this one and is still down being looked at by the Everton medical team, the Ukrainian has a very nasty cut as a result of the incident..
Dyche is in discussions with assistant Ian Woan about possible options if he has to come off here.
Mykolenko does carry on after extensive checks and returns to action with a lot of strapping around his head.
It brings back memories of Terry Butcher (only not quite so much blood).
Oh dear.
Everton have the chance to put a free-kick forward.
Garner takes it short to Harrison, who just dinks it straight into the hands of Martinez.
What a waste!
A Villa breakaway ultimately leads to a corner, which is taken short.
Luiz delivers but Everton deal with the danger with ease.
CLOSE! It's been a very scrappy affair in the second half, not helped by the stoppage for Mykolenko.
But McGinn has a chance centrally from just outside the goal and bends a left-footed effort just wide of the left-hand post.
Diaby wanted a penalty for a foul from Tarkowski in the build-up but never in a million years was it a foul.
Up at the other end Danjuma has a chance to swing a leg at one but it's not the best effort and it goes harmlessly wide of the right-hand post.
Dyche opts to roll the dice.
Calvert-Lewin, who really should have a goal to his name today, is replaced up front by Beto.
It's a double change for the Toffees with Danjuma, who in all honesty has done little to affect the game, is replaced by McNeil.
Emery is making some tactical switches to his forward line and as such Bailey, who hasn't done a great deal, comes off for Duran.
The ineffective Diaby is Villa's second man to be subbed off.
The flying forward doesn't look impressed but he has to take a seat as Tielemans - back after a month on the sidelines with a calf injury - enters the fray.
This one certainly hasn't been a bad game by any stretch, but there have been some lull periods and some sloppy moments that have prevented a pattern emerging.
There'll be at least another 30 minutes to play here, can anyone grab the initiative?
Unai Emery is currently averaging 2.02 points-per-game in the Premier League with Aston Villa (91 points in 45 games).
He is currently the only manager in Premier League history to manage 40+ games with a club and have an average of two or more points-per-game but not to have won the title with that side.
There's another break here as Onana goes down after a collision with Tielemans.
This one was in a rather more...sensitive...area.
A quick check, a quick count and we're back underway.
The aftermath of the kerfuffle caused by Tarkowski's challenge on Moreno leads to Lenglet being cautioned for his reaction.
Tarkowski goes into the book for a bit of an overzealous challenge on Moreno having been frustrated at being held by Carlos.
It all leads to a bit of pushing and shoving, which is quite in fitting with a game that is starting to show a bit of needle.
Emery opts to make a third sub as Carlos comes off for Cash, Villa's match-winner in the FA Cup against Middlesbrough last time out.
This one is just getting a bit scrappy now and Tielemans, having moments earlier lost possession in a dangerous area on the right, clumsily takes down Garner.
It leads to a big reaction from the Goodison crowd but it's not malicious.
Moreno, who has a very good game, swings in a dangerous ball from the left flank.
Duran has two attempts with the head but the second just floats harmlessly into the hands of Pickford.
Tielemans this time puts one in from the left and Branthwaite has to be alert to the danger, which he is and Everton get the ball away.
Officially we're into the final 10 minutes, but you have to assume there's going to be a large chunk of injury time added on.
Still plenty of time for a winner.
For most of the game Villa have looked to attack down the left and again they do as Moreno crosses in.
There's a bit of afters as Duran looks to push slightly on the injured head of Mykolenko, which leads to Branthwaite giving the Villa forward a little shove of his own.
Again it's down the Villa left and again it's Moreno who delivers low.
Mykolenko does brilliantly to get across quickly and slide in to block from Cash.
Plenty of huffing, plenty of puffing, but so far just absolutely no knocking down the door.
CHANCE! It's down the Villa right this time as substitute Cash gets down the flank and plays into the area where Duran gets the touch but it goes wide of the left-hand post.
Agonising stuff!
GOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOO-NO!! This time it's Everton who think they have the winner! It's played forward from deep and Doucoure races through into the penalty area.
He fires a left-footed effort past Martinez, Goodison Park roars its approval, but the linesperson's flag is up and it's still 0-0!

events.action: fires a left-footed effort past Martinez

text: Another roll of the dice from Emery here as McGinn comes off to be replaced by Zaniolo.
It's not quite as much as the first half but the fourth official's board shows there will be a minimum of seven minutes added on here at Goodison Park.
This one is just starting to peter out a little, it's not been a classic in the second half, more attritional.
Again down the left, again Moreno (it's like Groundhog Day).
The full-back floats one in and Duran nods wide of the right post.
He was backtracking in fairness and couldn't generate the power required.
We're into the final minute of the additional time now, can anyone snatch this right at the death?
FULL-TIME: EVERTON 0-0 ASTON VILLA
That's all she wrote at Goodison Park and it finishes goalless between Everton and Aston Villa.
In truth, you have to say it was a fair result - the close nature of the match was reflected in the xG with Everton's 1.13 slightly higher than Villa's 1.11.
There were definitely opportunities for both teams to win it, not least for Calvert-Lewin who really should have buried his chance when played through one-on-one at the end of the opening period.
Villa did have the ball in the back of the net before that through the excellent Moreno, who was denied after a lengthy VAR check.
The second half really failed to ignite and became a bit scrappy and needly, so really a point apiece is a fair reflection of the afternoon's proceedings.
It means Everton are one point clear of 18th-placed Luton Town but they have played a game more.
Villa, meanwhile, remain third in the table, two back of leaders Liverpool and level with Manchester City in second - both of whom have played one game fewer.
Thank you for joining this afternoon!
